A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFLS detector using RT, LT and RLT. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v5 reports original detection experiments, adaptive-attack evaluations, ablations, CNN/ViT results and benign-noise tests.

after.justification: v6 retains original experiments and adds gradient measurements, calibration studies, distribution-shift evaluations and direct AFLS analyses.

M1.justification: The RT/LT/RLT architecture is retained, but the scoring specification is refined: RT consistently uses the recovered-layer count L−kRT, LT gains numerical safeguards, and RLT uses clipped empirical-CDF transforms. Section 2.6 also introduces an explicit order-statistic threshold rule. These are limited scoring and calibration changes.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and the adversarial-detection task are retained. Beyond v5's random-noise tests, v6 adds benign brightness, contrast, blur, pixelation, crop and horizontal-flip scenarios in Appendices J and L. This broadens input conditions within the existing image domain.

E2.justification: Matched standard-attack, adaptive-attack, computational-cost and ViT comparisons retain the same comparator sets. This includes the existing BEYOND, Mao, neighborhood-based detectors and ViT LID comparisons; the new diagnostics introduce no competing detector.

E3.justification: New studies introduce disjoint auxiliary-fitting, CDF-fitting, threshold-calibration and evaluation samples; gradient measurements on 1,000 clean and 1,000 successful PGD inputs; and paired AFLS measurements across 12 dataset/model combinations. Figure 5 also changes its stated normalization reference from clean test samples to designated benign CDF-fitting samples. These descriptions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D.5, J and L add direct gradient-alignment diagnostics, calibration-size and benign-coverage sensitivity, target-domain recalibration, AFLS amplification/concentration measurements and complementary LT detections. These substantially expand tests of mechanisms and failure conditions beyond the retained component, perturbation-budget and noise analyses.

E5.justification: Beyond v5's repeated-run means and standard deviations, v6 adds 100 calibration resamples with 95th-percentile reporting, a 95% Wilson interval for held-out FPR, 20-resample auxiliary calibration analyses, and gradient medians/IQRs. These substantially expand statistical validation without implying additional training runs for retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and transfer scores are retained, but substantial results are added: AFLS exceedance averages 87.51% for attacks versus 3.57% for benign transformations (Table 35), and pixelation FPR falls from 78.78% to 4.88% after recalibration (Table 30). Gradient and calibration results are also new. v5 Table 26's extra Lower Bound result column is removed in v6 Table 27.

T1.justification: AFLS receives explicit amplification, benign-reference and concentration definitions. Appendices B–C replace the probabilistic RT argument and inferred LT instability with explicit sufficient conditions and revised proofs, and distinguish population from empirical CDFs. Appendix H corrects robustness accounting and the lower-bound proof; Appendix J adds a finite-sample FPR proposition under exchangeability.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace broad state-of-the-art claims covering strong adaptive attacks with positive performance claims focused on standard attacks and characterization of adaptive limitations. The first-to-formalize Lipschitz-violation contribution is replaced by direct empirical layer-shift measurement, and AFLS is explicitly framed as a setting-dependent hypothesis.

C2.justification: v6 withdraws the inherent RT–LT gradient-conflict explanation and speculative attack-to-layer causal narratives. It emphasizes low-FPR BPDA failures, variable gradient alignment, benign-shift false positives, exchangeability requirements and limited architectural validation. Appendix H now identifies independence as an approximation and explains when detection strictly improves system robustness.

D1.justification: v6 adds calibration sample allocations, CDF clipping instructions, the BPDA backward approximation, attack configurations in Appendix K and model-stage mappings in Table 36. Core training hyperparameters and code access remain. The earlier NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada hardware disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and almost all cited works remain. v6 removes Elfwing et al. (2018) and moderates novelty positioning by dropping the first-to-formalize claim and the assertion of a fundamentally different horizontal-versus-vertical paradigm.

P1.justification: Existing prose is extensively rewritten across the abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, experimental discussions, ablation interpretations and conclusion. Terminology is clarified, calibration gains a dedicated subsection, supporting material expands into new appendices, and author, affiliation and publication text changes.

P2.justification: The preprint is reformatted into the TMLR layout, with substantial table and figure relocation and different text wrapping. v6 adds multipanel Figures 6–7 and diagnostic, calibration and configuration tables. Existing captions and labels are revised, and the system-bound table loses one column.

improvement.justification: v6 resolves important weaknesses in v5's reasoning and overinterpretation through explicit conditional proofs, corrected system-robustness accounting and narrower claims. New AFLS, gradient and calibration studies directly test the proposed explanations and expose deployment failures that the revised limitations acknowledge. These substantially improve scientific reliability despite largely unchanged benchmark scores and some remaining unspecified attack defaults.
